scope: Each entry describes one mutation, separately, over reachable healthy frozen-s3 states and canonical model input domains; the 27 individually configured faults are tested, not universally proved. Structural/commit invariants sampled in scratch/s3/equivalence-{core,correction,g,mis,operations}; core R1 with obsolete savedAckEcho failed and is superseded by correction. Samples support the accompanying arguments, not exhaustive proofs. Frozen Lean guarantee supplies healthy monotonic-permission facts. Domain and unused-alias survivors are unreachable; constructor/name cases are syntactic equivalents.

H002.argument: Without typed input or risk, every held page has buf == base; NOPAGE does too. Init establishes this; submit sets typed, uncertain/conflict sets risk, Published/discard establish equality.

H004.argument: Risk implies held. Every retirement installs NOPAGE, which is clean, so !held is redundant in clean-or-risk and risk predicates.

H020.argument: The locked page's promise cannot outrun its save job. An active same-version draft acknowledgement repeats bytes/ep; an active same-version saved acknowledgement repeats the saved record. Upgrade requires pr.on; an ended promise may retain different historical bytes, and is excluded. Each individual removal is either still rejected or repeats the original record.

H205.argument: At a healthy phase-2 save with guard true and bytes != base, the base is already seen or in opRead. Window input exposes its predecessor; CLI operations record the base they read, including ABSENT. H342.argument: While a healthy save job is active its page remains held and dirty. opDelete independently requires opClean on that page, so the job's page cannot pass even without opFree. Flush starts dirty; guarded observe/delivery/operations cannot change the locked page; completion or lifecycle clears the job atomically. Four 4096x40 samples support jobDirty. The explicit lock remains in the transcription and is an implementation obligation.
